findings.text: the after_suite record names revision 23b732f339c8085d9e132063b1c23023ab45991b while the reviewed worktree head is a31078e748c9bee098d1451f8d6cecf42fbd5d7c (a fragment-correction commit), so the stored after arm ties the 30-passed gate to a revision one commit behind the head a reader selects the record by; the intervening commit changes only the fragment, and I re-ran the three-file gate at 23b732f3 (the code head) and reproduced 30 passed/EXIT=0, so the verdict holds -- but from the record alone the after arm's revision is not the reviewed head.

the wider lane-named regression set (28 files) is measured in gate-support.log only at the intermediate fragment commit 4c98fb00 (5 failed, 245 passed), and at the final head 23b732f3 only the timestamp pin was re-run (gate-support-head.log); the four non-pin failures are recorded at base by the predecessor fragment lane-counts-read-through-the-lane-document.html, so no new id is expected, but the routing rework's blast radius is not itself re-measured at the final head -- it rests on the three-file gate plus the one source that reads the document's keys. Outside this node's measure.

read_lane_reading_fields returns the detail "lane document carries no parseable 'observed_at' timestamp" for a document that is not a JSON object, which misnames the failure -- the same class of message the carry gives a missing or non-string stamp (line 467), so an object-shaped failure reads as a stamp-shaped one. The function's own docstring says a non-object "resolves as a reading carrying no stamp", so the contract and the message disagree. It is unreachable through dispatch today because _lane_reading_carry guards the non-Mapping case first with a dispatch-endorsed detail ("lane document is X, not a JSON object)."); low severity, and no live path is affected.

justifications.durability: The guarded thing is made to happen and the refusal is shown, and I reproduced both directions. With read_lane_counts mutated to return a literal 0 as the generating count, the parity case passes in a scratch tree cut from base (1 passed, EXIT=0) and fails at head (1 failed, EXIT=1, assertion {'generating': 0} != {'generating': 7} at tests/test_lane_reading_carries_counts.py:263) -- which is the defect being repaired, shown to be repaired. The new sentinel case is also discriminating rather than decorative: with dispatch.py mutated to spell the document's keys directly in place of the read_lane_reading_fields call, test_the_dispatch_carries_what_the_document_readers_resolved reddens (1 failed, EXIT=1, the carried observed_at is the document's stamp rather than the sentinel's). Docked one because the sentinel patches only the two readers the carry calls, so a future direct spell of headroom (read through read_lane_document) would not be caught by it, and because the repair's own negative control tests one mutation. Every arm ran under the pinned interpreter with the module under test proven by a field the run declares; no unrelated suite is claimed.
justifications.evidence: Both suite objects carry revision, command, exit_status, completed, failure_count and failure_ids, and added_failure_count 0 with no ids follows from the logs: gate-base.log ends '29 passed in 15.81s / EXIT=0' and gate-head.log ends '30 passed in 17.57s / EXIT=0', matching the manifest's failure_count 0 / [] on both arms. I reproduced both arms myself (same summary lines, EXIT=0 at each) and reproduced the negative-control pair (base-mutated 1 passed/EXIT=0; head-mutated 1 failed/EXIT=1). Docked two: (1) after_suite names revision 23b732f33 while the reviewed worktree head is a31078e7, a follow-up fragment-correction commit, so the stored after arm ties the 30-passed gate to a revision one commit behind the head a reader selects the record by -- the intervening commit is docs/evidence only and I re-ran the gate at the code head, so the verdict holds, but the stored arm's revision is not the reviewed head. (2) the wider lane-named regression set (28 files) was measured only at the intermediate fragment commit 4c98fb00 (gate-support.log: 5 failed/245 passed) and re-run at the final head only for the timestamp pin (gate-support-head.log), so the blast radius of the routing rework is covered at the final head by the three-file gate plus that single pin; the four non-pin failures are recorded at base by the predecessor fragment, so no new id is expected -- but the wider set was not itself re-measured at head.
justifications.fit: The change follows the module's own idiom: read_lane_reading_fields joins read_lane_counts and read_lane_throughput in lane_document.py and the carry calls it instead of reading the document, and the coercion helpers are bytes-equivalent -- lane_document._number and dispatch._metric_number have the same body (bool rejected, non-numeric to None), so routing mean_context through _number is semantics-preserving, and the blank-binding rule (blank string to None) is carried over verbatim. No plan label, version, ticket or author attribution appears in any staged path, filename, symbol or comment. ruff check over the three changed paths returns the same seven pre-existing findings at base (33c5e761d) and at head, all in reckon/crew/dispatch.py and none in the region this change touches, and ruff format --check lists the same single file at both revisions.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The followup f-cot-lane-counts-parity-and-remaining-names is discharged and I reproduced both halves independently. The parity case (tests/test_lane_reading_carries_counts.py:263) no longer compares the payload against a second reading of the same document: each fixture entry now carries the counts it states as a literal and BOTH read_lane_counts(written) and the payload's generating/waiting are held against that literal, so the two sides have independent provenance. The four document keys the carry still spelled -- observed_at, mean_context, binding_observed, suggested_shelf_life_seconds -- now resolve through lane_document.read_lane_reading_fields; grep -c 'document\.get(' reckon/crew/dispatch.py is 0 at head, and the only document-derived read left in the carry is read_lane_document(document).get('headroom'), which was already routed. I re-ran the three-file gate in scratch trees cut from 33c5e761d and from HEAD: 29 passed/EXIT=0 at base, 30 passed/EXIT=0 at head, reproducing the manifest. The new case test_the_dispatch_carries_what_the_document_readers_resolved patches both readers to sentinels and requires the payload to carry them, so the composition is proven to come from the readers. The plan's still-open per-row-rate half is correctly left untouched.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 33c5e761d a31078e7 lists four paths -- docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/lane-counts-parity.html, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/lane_document.py and tests/test_lane_reading_carries_counts.py -- every one inside the manifest's five declared write paths; the declared docs/figures path (a figure this node's done-write names none of) is correctly untouched, and the fragment it authors is this node's own evidence file. The worker committed locally on the worktree head with conventional subject and body, did not mutate the plan, index or sprint state, and ran each arm under the pinned interpreter with a private /tmp basetemp. No write outside the granted paths.
